label: Highest tide today
how: Highest astronomical tide at Outer Harbor: 2.847 m above the port's chart datum (lowest astronomical tide), which is 1.452 m below AHD, so 1.395 m AHD, rounded to 1.4
source: Tonkin Consulting, Stormwater Management Plan Glenelg to Marino (City of Holdfast Bay and City of Marion, July 2014), Table 2.3; chart datum offset from Bureau of Meteorology station metadata for Outer Harbor (61600) and Adelaide's Living Beaches Technical Report (DEH 2005), p. 30. AusTides 2017 gives 2.8 m LAT (1.35 m AHD).

label: Highest tide + 0.3 m
how: The highest tide plus the Coast Protection Board's 0.3 m allowance for sea level rise to 2050
source: Coast Protection Board Policy Document, revised October 2022, Appendix 1: 'a mid-range sea level rise of 0.3m by the year 2050 be adopted for most coastal planning and design'

label: Highest tide + 1.0 m
how: The highest tide plus the Board's 1.0 m allowance to 2100
source: Coast Protection Board Policy Document, revised October 2022, Appendix 1: 'The Board has adopted a 1m rise to 2100 for coastal policy'

label: 1-in-100-year storm tide + 0.3 m
how: The 1% AEP (1-in-100-year) still water storm tide for the metropolitan coast, 2.4 m AHD, plus 0.3 m: the basis of the Board's standard for building sites to 2050 (before any local adjustment for subsidence). Wave setup and run-up are not in it.
source: Adelaide's Living Beaches Technical Report (Department for Environment and Heritage, 2005), p. 100: 'the 1-in-100 year average return interval storm surge level of 2.4 m AHD'; Coast Protection Board Policy Document (October 2022), Standard S1. Outer Harbor's own 1% AEP level is given as 2.325 to 2.38 m AHD and the Inner Harbor's as 2.50 m AHD (City of Port Adelaide Enfield, 2005, cited in WRL TR 2022/15 Table 3.4 and Tonkin 2014 Table 2.4).

label: 1-in-100-year storm tide + 1.0 m
how: The same storm tide plus the Board's 1.0 m to 2100
